transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Well, I suppose it’s mostly that my head has been feeling a bit foggy lately. I’m probably making it sound worse than it is, but I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, dates for exhibits, and even which volunteer I already called. It’s embarrassing, really. I thought maybe I should come in and ask about it… if that’s the right thing to do.
How long have you been experiencing this foggy feeling and memory difficulty? Has it been getting worse over time?

I think it’s been… about four months now. It seemed to start around when we had the water damage and got pushed into all that remodeling. I don’t want to make too much of it, but since then I’ve noticed the fogginess more. I’m not sure if I’d say it’s dramatically worse, but it hasn’t really gone away.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in activities you usually enjoy?

A little, yes… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic. But things I usually love—my watercolors, fussing over my tomato plants, going line dancing, even just watching the cardinals out back—lately they just sort of sit there. I look at them and I can’t quite make myself care the way I used to. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels lately, or do you often feel tired or fatigued even after resting?

Yes… I suppose I have been more tired than usual. I do sleep, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t quite rested, if that makes sense. And then just washing up and making myself some breakfast can wear me out enough that I feel like I ought to sit down again. I’m not sure if that’s normal at my age, but it has been noticeable.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately?

A little, yes… not on purpose or anything. Food just hasn’t sounded very appealing most days, so I’ll sort of pick at some toast or maybe soup and call that enough. And I have noticed my skirts are fitting looser than they used to. I don’t think it’s a huge amount, but… it’s there.
Have you noticed yourself moving slower than usual, or perhaps thinking more slowly than you normally do?

Yes… I think so. I wasn’t sure if it was worth mentioning, but my husband says I move like I’m wading through mud these days. Even little things, like getting up to answer the phone or sorting through the mail, seem to take me such a long time. I’m not trying to be difficult, it just feels… slower than it ought to.
Have you found yourself feeling worthless, guilty, or thinking about death or dying more often lately?

I don’t think so… not in any serious way. I mean, I suppose I can be hard on myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t want to make more of it than it is. I haven’t been sitting around thinking about death, if that’s what you mean. Is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
Have you ever felt like you're seeing or hearing things that others don't, or have you had any thoughts that you know aren't true but are hard to let go of?

No… I don’t believe so. I mean, I forget things now and then, but I haven’t been hearing voices or seeing things that other people don’t see. And I don’t think I’ve had thoughts like that… not ones I knew weren’t true. Is that all right?
Have there been any other major changes or stressful events in your life recently that have been weighing on you?

Well… yes, I suppose there has been. We had some water damage at the house, and it sort of pushed us into this remodel. It’s been going on about four months now, and I don’t mean to complain—people have worse problems—but it has been weighing on me more than I expected.
Have you found that you no longer enjoy activities you used to like, or do they feel like more of a chore than they used to be?

I suppose… yes, a bit. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but things I used to really enjoy—my watercolors, my tomato plants, even line dancing—just sort of sit there now. I look at them and think I should do something, but I can’t quite make myself care. Even watching the cardinals out back doesn’t feel the same. Is that what you mean?
Have you found it difficult to follow a conversation, keep track of your finances, or handle other everyday tasks that you used to manage easily?

Yes… that’s actually part of why I came in, though I feel a little embarrassed saying it. My head just feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things I normally would have straight—appointment times, exhibit dates, or whether I already called a certain volunteer. It’s not that I can’t do anything, exactly, but I’m making more little mistakes than I used to. Does that make sense?
Would you say that most days, you feel down or sad for most of the day, or that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in most activities for a period of at least two weeks?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say, at least about the interest part. I don’t want to overstate it, but things I used to love—my watercolors, my tomato plants, line dancing, even just watching the cardinals out back—they mostly just sit there now. I keep thinking I should pick them up again, but I can’t seem to make myself care the way I used to.
Have you noticed any worsening in your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or remember things over the past few months?

Yes… I have noticed that. That’s really one of the things that brought me in, though I feel a little silly admitting it. My head just feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates, and even which volunteer I already called. It’s not terrible, but it’s more than usual for me, if that makes sense.
Have you ever experienced a time where you believed something strongly that others didn't share, even when it was clear to them it wasn't true?

Well… I’m not sure if this is what you mean, and I don’t want it to sound silly or grand. But there was a time I honestly felt like I was the one person who could turn our senior center into something people from all over town would come to see. I really believed I could make it into something special, maybe more strongly than other people seemed to think was realistic.
Would you say that most days, you feel like you can’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even things that made you happy before?

Yes… yes, I think so. I don’t mean I never enjoy anything at all, but most days it’s like the feeling just isn’t there. My watercolors are sitting untouched, the tomato plants too, and I used to love line dancing and watching the cardinals out back. Now I’ll think, “That should make me happy,” but I just can’t seem to make myself care about it the way I did.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a major depressive episode characterized by persistent depressed mood, loss of interest or pleasure, fatigue, psychomotor slowing, impaired concentration, and reduced appetite with weight loss. These symptoms have been present for over four months and are associated with functional impairment in daily tasks. There is no evidence of prolonged or maladaptive reaction to a psychosocial stressor severe enough to meet criteria for adjustment disorder with depressed mood, making major depressive disorder the most accurate diagnosis.
